final_message:
I found and fixed 7 bugs. All 24 tests now pass (8 failed before), and I didn't change any tests. `REPORT.md` has one line per bug in the format you asked for.

| File | Function | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amounts.py` | `parse_amount` | `(12.50)` style amounts lost their parentheses but stayed positive. | Parentheses now make the amount negative. |
| `amounts.py` | `parse_amount` | The number was passed straight to `Decimal`, so it accepted things the README doesn't allow: `1e3`, `1_000`, `12,34`, `+5`. `-$-12` even came back as **+12**. | The number must now be digits, with optional comma thousands and an optional decimal part. Anything else raises `ValueError`. |
| `currency.py` | `convert` | The rates were applied the wrong way round. | Now goes A → EUR → B, rounding once at the end. |
| `currency.py` | `minor_units` | Looked up `"jpy"` in a table keyed `"JPY"`, so yen got 2 decimals instead of 0. | Now uses the same case-insensitive code check as `convert`. |
| `vat.py` | `vat_rate_for` | Ignored case and whitespace, so `"Books"` or `" food "` got the standard 20%. | Category is trimmed and lower-cased before lookup. |
| `invoice.py` | `line_total` | VAT was charged on the amount before discount. | VAT is now charged on the discounted net. |
| `dates.py` | `days_in_range` | Left out the end date, so every range was one day short. | End date is now included. |

I also spot-checked cases outside the tests, including `($1,200.00)`, `-$12.50`, `$-12.50`, `-0.005`, garbage strings, USD→JPY and JPY→GBP conversions, and mixed-case VAT categories.

One thing I left alone: if `round_money` or `line_total` are given Python floats instead of strings or `Decimal`, they inherit float inaccuracy (e.g. `round_money(2.675)` gives `2.67`). The README says all money is `Decimal`, so I treated float input as outside the rules rather than a bug.
